Profile Fanny Arlandis Subscribers only Nour Elassy, Gaza-born poet and refugee in France: 'I live with the guilt of having left my loved ones behind' In 2025, the 23-year-old student left her family in the enclave after Israel approved her evacuation, allowing her to attend classes in Paris. She recently published a poetry collection evoking a world engulfed by the destruction of the Palestinian territory. 5 min read

In Depth Clément Guillou and Corentin Lesueur Subscribers only French far right gets tangled up in headscarf ban proposal Intended as a communications coup, the revival of the long-standing debate within the Rassemblement National over banning the headscarf in public spaces has exposed legal uncertainties and disagreements between Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella. 4 min read

Interview Subscribers only Anne-Cécile Mailfert, president of Fondation Des Demmes: 'For the first time, perhaps, a gender-violence bill was shaped from the victims' perspective' In an interview with Le Monde, Anne-Cécile Mailfert, who participated in the discussions behind this legislative proposal, explains its origins, contents and how it came to be included on the parliamentary agenda following the death of 11-year-old Lyhanna.

Editorial Addressing rape culture to better denounce it In an investigation into a case of sexual violence under the guise of 'libertinism,' Le Monde reports on acts described by prosecutors as rapes 'with torture and acts of barbarity.' It is not an isolated incident, but rather a symptom of a wider online male culture that hides behind the language of consent and 'sexual plurality.'

Gallery Subscribers only Behind the scenes of Macron's last G7, as told by photographer Kamil Zihnioglu There is protocol, and then there is Donald Trump. That, in essence, is what photographer Kamil Zihnioglu took away from his three days covering the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains for Le Monde.

Letter from... Subscribers only 'Thank you, dear Hungary, for proving that anything is always possible' Jean-Baptiste Chastand, Le Monde's Central Europe correspondent, writes a letter to this 'hostile and surprising' country he has covered for more than 10 years.

From the Archive Subscribers only Marjane Satrapi's comic strips for Le Monde, 20 years ago Best known for her masterpiece 'Persepolis,' the French-Iranian graphic novelist and filmmaker, who died on June 4, published comic strips in issues of Le Monde's magazine.
News Groupe Le Monde's ownership structure in 2026 Since 2010, Groupe Le Monde's capital structure has gone through several changes and is now stable.

News Groupe Le Monde posts stable revenue and profits in 2025 With revenue of €306.2 million, Groupe Le Monde's 2025 accounts, approved on May 19, reflect a robustness that demonstrates the effectiveness of a strategy implemented for more than a decade.
Document Le Monde RSS feeds This page contains Le Monde's various RSS feeds, which allow you to follow all our coverage.

Your stories Subscribers only 'I don't recognize any faces': Yohann's life with prosopagnosia From childhood, Yohann Cordelle learned to navigate his prosopagnosia: a little-known neurological disorder that makes it impossible to remember faces. Now in his forties, he shares the coping strategies he has put in place.
Molly Le Corre and Héloïse Robert, students at Sciences Po Rennes

News AI: Meta signs partnership agreement with several international media outlets, including Le Monde The contract regulates the use of content published by Le Monde, Télérama, Huffington Post and Nouvel Obs in artificial intelligence services developed by the American group, owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.
Explainer How to securely contact Le Monde's investigations team Here are the steps you can follow to securely send information of public interest to Le Monde's investigative journalists.

Document Le Monde Group's 2025 institutional report This document is filled with everything you have ever wanted to know about the Le Monde Group, detailing the identity, values, governance, audience, and business model of the group's publications.

News Le Monde Group's 2024 accounts mark a landmark year The steady growth in digital readership across the group's publications, the awards received by our titles and new partnerships in artificial intelligence have further strengthened our editorial and business strategy.

Explainer Artificial intelligence: Le Monde signs partnership agreement with Perplexity The multi-year agreement signed with the American company will improve the quality of information in its answer engine and provide the editorial team with innovative tools, while ensuring the protection of its rights and the remuneration of its content.

Op-Ed In the US, 47 journalists' associations denounce attacks on freedom of expression Led by the Society of Professional Journalists, 47 American journalists' societies and associations are calling on the Trump administration to lift its ban on the Associated Press, which recently lost access to the White House. Le Monde's Association of Journalists lends its support.

Editorial Introducing M International: The best of Le Monde's M magazine, now in English From March on, the best of M Le magazine du Monde will be available online, in a biannual print edition and twice a month as a newsletter.

Op-Ed Le Monde's Association of Journalists condemns the revocation of our Moscow correspondent's accreditation The Russian authorities have decided to revoke the accreditation of Le Monde correspondent Benjamin Quénelle. This decision brings to an end almost 70 years of Le Monde's presence in Russia.
Editorial To our readers: On Le Monde's correspondent being banned from working in Russia

Selection Le Monde in English's playlist of the French hits that should have made it to the Olympics opening ceremony Because the Paris Olympics and its opening and closing ceremonies were such big news events for Le Monde in English, we thought we would keep the magic going into the New Year.

News Subscribers only Le Monde turns 80: A decade of novelty and innovation Since 2014, the newspaper has experienced a veritable revolution in how it covers the news. The newsroom has created around 20 new events, supplements or formats. Video, particularly vertical video, has grown considerably.

In Depth 80 years of Le Monde: Your questions answered about how our newsroom works 'Who chooses the story?' 'Does artificial intelligence affect your job?' 'How long to write an article?': Le Monde's editorial team answered readers' questions as the newspaper celebrated its 80th anniversary on Wednesday, December 18.

In Depth Subscribers only 80 years of Le Monde: An unprecedented editorial independence in French media Le Monde Group's Independence Hub, which is made up of shareholding employees, has the power to veto the entry of a new controlling shareholder.
Editorial 80 years of Le Monde: Evolutions in keeping with our identity and values The newspaper is celebrating its 80th birthday with the pride of having become France's leading national daily.

In Graphs Which countries have appeared most on Le Monde's front page, and when? The newspaper's 24,856 front pages since 1944 to 2024 retrace the last eight decades of major upheavals around the world.

News Subscribers only Two Le Monde journalists awarded top journalism prize Lorraine de Foucher, in the print media category, and Martin Untersinger, for books, share the honor of the prestigious Prix Albert Londres with Antoine Védeilhé and Germain Baslé, for video.
Q&A Article in live How the US elections are seen and covered in France? Your questions answered Our former correspondent in Washington, Gilles Paris, answered your questions live.

Long Read Subscribers only How Le Monde has covered race in the US When Le Monde was founded 80 years ago, it quickly picked up on racism in the United States as a key issue to watch. In its early days, the newspaper denounced segregation, while using offensive language to talk about Black Americans.

Gallery Subscribers only The war in Lebanon through the lens of a Le Monde photographer: 'People are traumatized by the bombings and the pager attack' On September 24, photographer Adrienne Surprenant landed in Beirut. Three days later, an Israeli strike killed Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah. Surprenant tells us about her work for Le Monde in Lebanon and the challenges posed by the conflict.

News Subscribers only How Le Monde covers the Israel-Hamas war A dozen journalists from Le Monde's international desk are reporting on events that are unprecedented in the ongoing Middle Eastern conflict in terms of scale, but also in terms of working conditions.

Op-Ed French journalist associations again demand access to Gaza Le Monde's Association of Journalists, along with many others, is calling on international bodies and the leaders of all countries to call for this territory to be opened to the press so that it can do its job to inform.

Long Read Subscribers only How Le Monde covered space, from the first rockets to the SpaceX revolution The founding of the newspaper in 1944 coincided with the launch of the first rockets to space. Science immediately found its way into Le Monde, from Sputnik, the first man in space, missions to the Moon, the Apollo programs and the Ariane epic.

News Le Monde's festival celebrates the paper's 80th anniversary with debates, concerts and more Le Monde is celebrating its 80th anniversary (and the 10th anniversary of the Le Monde festival!) from September 19 to 22, 2024.

Long Read Subscribers only The long battle for climate coverage in Le Monde It took the determination of a few pioneering reporters in the 1970s, alarming IPCC reports from 1990 onward, and young journalists' boldness for environmental issues to carve out a place among political and international topics in Le Monde's pages. With some mockery along the way.

Profile Subscribers only Jean-Paul Descombey, Le Monde's most loyal reader from day one The 94-year-old French psychiatrist-psychoanalyst has never stopped reading the newspaper since it was first published on December 18, 1944, even if occasional articles have sometimes exasperated him.
Round-up Paris 2024: How to follow the Olympics with Le Monde in English Here's a look at the special coverage we have planned for the duration of the Games, and how you can best follow along.

Long Read Subscribers only Le Monde and the Olympics, an irresistible combination In 1948, at the Winter Olympics held in Saint-Moritz, Switzerland, the management of Le Monde agreed to send one journalist to cover the events. In 2024, in Paris, the event has become a must for the newspaper, and nearly a hundred of its journalists are involved.

Long Read Subscribers only Le Monde and Europe, a quintessentially French history Throughout its 80-year history, Le Monde has proclaimed its European convictions, but without making Europe the beating heart of its editorial line.

Long Read Subscribers only French cinematic history through the lens of Le Monde's critics From post-war films to the streaming revolution and #MeToo, Le Monde critics have always examined the evolution of French cinema and its production conditions.

Long Read Subscribers only How Le Monde has covered the Israeli-Palestinian conflict since 1945 Since the founding of Le Monde in late 1944, the newspaper's coverage and editorial position have continuously fueled suspicions among readers: Pro-Israeli? Pro-Palestinian? Every article is dissected and discussed with a zeal not seen with any other international issue.

Long Read From de Gaulle to Macron, Le Monde's complicated relationship with French presidents France's 'paper of reference' has had mixed relations with each of the eight presidents of the Fifth Republic, trying to balance its role as a counter-power and the delicate task of expressing a position ahead of elections.

News Le Monde Group: Press releases from the Independence Pole and the Fund for the Independence of the Press The Le Monde Group's Independence Pole welcomes the acquisition by the Fund for the Independence of the Press of Xavier Niel's holding company NJJ Presse, which, via Le Monde Libre, controls the majority of the Le Monde Group's capital as well as Le Nouvel Obs.

News Journalism and Crisis: Join Le Monde in English for a special event in New York! Le Monde's English edition crosses the Atlantic from April 15-17 for a series of events in New York City, free and open to the public.

Editorial Le Monde and OpenAI sign partnership agreement on artificial intelligence This multi-year agreement, the first between a French media organization and a major AI player, will enable OpenAI to draw on our newspaper's corpus to establish and enhance the reliability of the answers of its ChatGPT tool, in return for a significant source of additional revenue.

News Le Monde adopts a charter on artificial intelligence The document lays down a strict framework for the use of AI by the press group's titles and states that generative artificial intelligence 'can in no way replace editorial teams.'

Long Read Subscribers only Le Monde and women: From the right to vote to #MeToo When women voted for the first time in France in 1945, the newspaper had no female editors and wrote only a few lines on the issue. Eighty years later, everything has changed: There are as many women as men in key positions, and equality issues are widely addressed.

Editorial Le Monde turns 80: The long history of our journalism and our commitments Through December 2024, Le Monde will be publishing a series of articles looking back on its 80-year history. Jérôme Fenoglio, our director, notes that our approach to covering the world's upheavals remains consistent with the one set forth by founder Hubert Beuve-Méry: journalism, nothing but journalism, and all journalism.

News Le Monde Group publishes its carbon footprint The press group's carbon footprint fell sharply in 2022 when compared with 2019, using the same metrics. The use of electronic devices to read the newspaper accounts for almost 40% of the total greenhouse gas emissions.

Selection Le Monde in English's gifts you can't buy The best gifts don't need to have a price tag. They can be about the time, thought, and love you put into them – which can also lower their carbon footprint.

Interview Fentanyl trafficking: 'Europe and the US must pressure banking havens that are essential for the cartels to launder their billions' Bertrand Monnet's investigation into fentanyl trafficking by Mexican cartels was published as Le Monde's three-part video series 'Narco Business.' The business school professor answered viewers' questions.

In Depth Subscribers only Israel-Hamas: How Le Monde navigates the image war This conflict, even more than others in the past, raises the question of where photos come from and how they are used. Whether for the newspaper's print or digital editions, Le Monde's editorial team is constantly faced with crucial choices.

Explainer Subscribers only The Gaza Strip: 20 years of Le Monde covering this increasingly inaccessible territory Correspondents describe the particular context of the Palestinian enclave, which despite experiencing four conflicts between 2008 and 2021, has received less attention from the media than the West Bank.

News To our readers: On Le Monde's coverage of the explosion at the Al Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza Le Monde looks back at the newsroom's coverage of the deadly explosion at the Al Ahli hospital in Gaza on October 17.

Editorial Two major milestones for Le Monde's independence Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky has sold his shares in Le Monde Group to Xavier Niel, who will transfer them to a foundation. Matthieu Pigasse has announced that his own shares will also be transferred to the same foundation, making it the group's largest shareholder.

News Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky sells Le Monde stake to Xavier Niel This agreement seals the tycoon's exit from the group's capital, which he joined in 2018. His shares will be transferred by Xavier Niel to the Press Independence Fund, which thus becomes the group's largest shareholder.

In Depth Adaptation project: How Le Monde calculated the carbon footprint of its reporting In the face of rapid climate change caused by human activity, it is our collective responsibility to measure and question the impact of how we travel.

News Le Monde presents the Adaptation project Over the coming five weeks, Le Monde is publishing an 11-chapter deep dive into the countless challenges that France faces to adapt to global warming. To face the great task of this century, the foundations must be laid now.
News Quiz: Test your 'Frenglish' with Le Monde in English! Can you translate the trickiest expressions used in French politics and everyday life − or even by President Emmanuel Macron himself?

News How 'Le Monde' in English translates between language and culture As Le Monde's English edition moves into its second year, our team takes you through the process of translating not only words but also culture from French to English.

News One year of 'Le Monde' in English Since its launch in April 2022, the English edition of 'Le Monde' has offered a selection of articles that reflect the richness of the French editorial staff's journalism.
Selection The top 20 articles you've read this year A mix of hard news, lighter pieces and all things French: Here are the stories you've most enjoyed this year.

interest</a></li></ul>             <h2 class="article__sub-title"><span id="huit-anchor-preamble"><strong>Preamble</strong></span></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">The purpose of this Code is to recall the essential principles of independence, freedom and reliability of information, and to specify the rights and obligations of journalists, executives, and shareholders. It will be binding on the parties (organizations or associations of journalists of the various titles, shareholders, Groupe Le Monde executives, directors of publications and newsrooms), and will be included in the articles of association of Groupe Le Monde companies. In the event of a change in leadership of one of the group's titles, it will be imposed in identical terms on their new editorial and publishing directors.</p>          <div id="inread_top" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread_top" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">This Code, which is shared by all Groupe Le Monde publications and sites, is an addition to the charters and agreements previously adopted by each of these titles. These texts, which are joined in an appendix to this Code, remain fully valid with the only exception of any of their provisions that may be contradictory with those of the present Code. Any change to this Code must be approved by a vote of the publications and is effective only in those publications that have actually approved it.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The vocation of Groupe Le Monde's titles is to provide, across all media, high-quality, accurate, verified and balanced information. Journalists must look at the news with a critical eye and reflect the pluralism of opinions.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Journalists have the means needed to carry out their work with attention to detail, to collect and verify information, independently of any external pressure. They refrain from manipulation and plagiarism, do not spread hearsay, and avoid sensationalism, approximations and bias. They must avoid any ties of interest with the actors in the sectors they report on, and undertake to declare any conflict of interest.</p>          <div id="inread" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The ethical principles shared by the newsrooms of Groupe Le Monde will be set out in an appendix to the Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, without any distinction in value or legal force with the content of the latter.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The editorial independence of Groupe Le Monde’s newspapers from its shareholders, advertisers, public, political, economic, ideological and religious authorities is the necessary condition for a free press and high-quality reporting. No text can be imposed on them, no direction can be dictated to them by an external intervention or constraint.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholders of Groupe Le Monde guarantee the economic independence of its titles within the meaning of the present Code, but refrain from interfering in their editorial choices and the way they handle information.</p>          <div id="inread-2" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The editorial policy of each title, whether in print or online, cannot be guided or influenced by the interests of advertisers, nor by those of other titles in the group. The editorial directors (or their delegates) are responsible for the editorial policy and content of their publication.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Within each title of Groupe Le Monde, there is a person responsible for the title’s economic equilibrium and management, who is separate from the person responsible for the editorial content. Under no circumstances may one of these two managers make a decision that affects the other's area of responsibility without the latter's agreement.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Two separate ethics and professional conduct committees, responsible respectively for the Le Monde daily newspaper, its supplements or variations, the Le Monde Interactif websites and its digital applications, on the one hand, and for all the magazines (the "Magazines Division") and their digital editions, on the other, are responsible for ensuring compliance with this Code.</p>          <div id="inread-3" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">In particular, they will ensure that all the principles contained in the Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists (Munich, 1971), which is essential to ensuring editorial independence and constitutes the ethical basis of the journalistic profession, are observed. These principles apply to the production of all editorial content produced by the group's newsrooms, regardless of the media used.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">This Code will be published in whole or in part in the various titles of the group as soon as it comes into force and will remain available in full and at any time on each of their websites.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Shareholders’ rights and obligations</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholders of Groupe Le Monde hold the powers conferred on them by corporate law. In this capacity, they oversee the smooth operations of the group and its publications, and help define its strategy and areas of development. To ensure the financial and political independence of the group's titles and sites, and to guarantee their independence and freedom of expression, each of them agrees to respect the values and principles defined in this Code.</p>          <div id="inread-4" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholders hereby attest to their commitment to the editorial independence of the group’s publications. They agree to respect this Code, as well as the specific charters in use in each of the group's newsrooms. Any new shareholder, whether majority or minority, will have to make the same commitment. The companies in Groupe Le Monde may only register movements or subscriptions of securities giving access to the capital in return for the adherence and signature of the present Code by their beneficiaries.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholders, their representatives and the members of the supervisory boards of Groupe Le Monde do not take part in editorial decisions. They attend editorial conferences only at the invitation of the newsroom or the newspaper's management, but may not speak at these meetings. They also refrain from commissioning an article and from giving instructions to modify an article or preventing it from being published.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholding structure of Groupe Le Monde will be published annually in paper and/or digital form by each of the Group's titles. At the same time, a report on the interests held by the main shareholders will also be provided.</p>          <div id="inread-5" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The shareholders agree not to impose commercial partnerships on the Group with companies they are shareholders in or which are tied to them through commercial relations. Similarly, they agree not to prevent or hinder similar partnerships with companies that are in competition with their own.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">When a shareholder of Groupe Le Monde or a company managed or owned by one of these shareholders is quoted in an article published by a title of Groupe Le Monde, this is indicated in the body of the article, in its title, or in a footnote.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Governance</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">Shareholders and members of the supervisory boards agree to ensure that, in the context of public expression, their statements may not be taken as the opinion of Groupe Le Monde, except in the case of a communication voted on by the supervisory board.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Membership in a Group Management Board is incompatible with:</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">- a national or local elective mandate (except for municipal mandates in cities with fewer than 30,000 residents)</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">- a management, supervisory or representative role within a political party or trade union</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">- a final prison sentence related to the following subjects: (i) incitement to racial hatred or discrimination; (ii) illicit financing of political parties; (iii) personal injury.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Journalists’ rights and obligations</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">This Code recognizes the Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists, adopted in Munich in 1971, in the following terms:</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Preamble</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The right to information, free expression and criticism is one of the most fundamental freedoms of every human being.</p>          <div id="inread-6" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The whole complex of duties and rights of journalists derives from this right of the public to know facts and opinions.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The responsibility of journalists vis-a-vis the public has precedence over any other responsibility, in particular towards their employers and the public power.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The mission to inform necessarily includes the limits journalists spontaneously impose on themselves. This is the subject of the present declaration of duties.</p>          <div id="inread-7" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Yet these duties can be effectively respected in the exercise of the journalist profession only if the concrete conditions of professional independence and dignity are implemented. This is the subject of the declaration of rights quoted here.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Declaration of Duties</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The essential duties of the journalist in gathering, reporting on and commenting on events consist in:</p>          <div id="inread-8" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">1) Respecting the truth no matter what consequences it may bring about to him, and this is because the right of the public is to know the truth.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">2) Defending the freedom of information, of commentaries and of criticism.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">3) Publishing only such pieces of information the origin of which is known or – in the opposite case – accompanying them with due reservations; not suppressing essential information and not altering texts and documents.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">4) Not making use of disloyal methods to get information, photographs and documents.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">5) Feeling obliged to respect the private life of people.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">6) Correcting any published information which has proved to be inaccurate.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">7) Observing professional secrecy and not divulging the source of information obtained confidentially.</p>          <div id="inread-9" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">8) Abstaining from plagiarism, slander, defamation and unfounded accusations as well as from receiving any advantage owing to the publication or suppression of information.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">9) Never confusing the profession of journalist with that of advertiser or propagandist and not accepting any consideration, direct or not, from advertisers.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">10) Refusing any pressure and accepting editorial directives only from the leading persons in charge in the editorial office.</p>          <div id="inread-10" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Every journalist worthy of that name deems it his duty faithfully to observe the principles stated above.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Within the general law of each country, the journalist recognizes, in professional matters, the jurisdiction of his colleagues only; he excludes every kind of interference by governments or others.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Declaration of Rights</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">1) Journalists claim free access to all information sources, and the right to freely inquire on all events conditioning public life.</p>          <div id="inread-11" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Therefore, secrecy of public or private affairs may be opposed only to journalists in exceptional cases and for clearly expressed motives.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">2) The journalist has the right to refuse subordination to anything contrary to the general policy of the information organ to which he collaborates such as it has been laid down in writing and incorporated in his contract of employment, as well as any subordination not clearly implicated by this general policy.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">3) A journalist cannot be compelled to perform a professional act or to express an opinion contrary to his convictions or his conscience.</p>          <div id="inread-12" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">4) The editorial staff has obligatorily to be informed on all important decisions which may influence the life of the enterprise.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">It should at least be consulted before a definitive decision on all matters related to the composition of the editorial staff, e.g. recruitment, dismissals, mutations and promotion of journalists, is taken.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">5) Taking into account his functions and responsibilities, the journalist is entitled not only to the advantages resulting from collective agreements but also to an individual contract of employment, ensuring the material and moral security of his work as well as a wage system corresponding to his social condition and guaranteeing his economic independence</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Advertising</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">In each of Groupe Le Monde's titles, whether in print or digital format, as well as in their supplements or special issues, editorial space and advertising or promotional space must be clearly and unambiguously marked. The typography, iconography and layout of advertising or advertorials must not be confused with the editorial content.</p>          <div id="inread-13" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Advertising imperatives cannot be invoked to influence the editorial choices of Groupe Le Monde's titles. Journalists may not contribute, even anonymously or free of charge, to the design, writing, illustration or layout of an advertisement or advertorial published in one of the group's titles.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Advertisers have no right to review or intervene in the content, including in supplements and special issues that they have helped to finance.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Brand protection</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">Groupe Le Monde's brands must not be used in a way that is incompatible with the Group's values. The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees shall assess and judge any risk of damage to the image of the brand concerned.</p>          <div id="inread-14" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">In the event of an agreement entailing a risk of this type, the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Société éditrice du Monde (SEM) (or, if it is separate from the SEM, the legal representative of the parent company of the Magazine Division) must refer the matter to the relevant Ethics Committee, within a period of time that will allow it to give its opinion before any irrevocable commitment is made. If this is not the case, any of its members may refer the matter to the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. The Committee may prohibit any use of the brand, outside the communication and media sector, which it considers detrimental to the image of the brand.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Role and power of journalists' organizations</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">An elected representative body, the board of the journalists' societies (SDJ) or their equivalent (journalists' associations, editors' organizations, etc.) of each publication has as its natural and permanent point of contact the editorial director of its title. In the event of a dispute, they may refer the matter to the appropriate Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">When faced with a problem of an ethical nature, any journalist has the right to refer the matter to her SDJ’s office so that it may become aware of it and submit it to the editorial director in order to find a solution. The editorial director and the publication director may also refer it to the SDJ office.</p>          <div id="inread-15" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The SDJ of a publication is informed in advance, within a reasonable period of time, of any decision relating to the development strategy of the title (in particular the creation or acquisition of a website, audiovisual support and a new product or a new activity). In the event of a proposed change of formula, the SDJ is informed by the editorial director or the publication director. In the event of proposed modifications to the production circuit, and after informing the elected representatives of the personnel, the editorial director will inform the relevant SDJ.</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Role and power of ethics and professional conduct committees</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">The purpose of the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees, to which the articles of association of the companies of Groupe Le Monde expressly refer, is to ensure compliance with this Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct within the Group’s various publications and sites. They do not have the authority to rule on the content of an article, nor to impose sanctions on journalists.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">In the event of a dispute over the interpretation or application of the Code, the matter may be referred to the relevant Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee by two of its members, by an SDJ, the editorial director or the chairman of the board of directors. Within one month of the referral, and after having interviewed the persons of its choice, the Committee shall issue an opinion and/or recommendations which will be communicated to the journalists concerned, to the management of the newsroom concerned and to the Chairman of the Board of Directors, and which may be published at its request. The management of the title concerned shall to respond in detail, and within fifteen days, to the opinion or recommendations of the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee.</p>          <div id="inread-16" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees shall be summoned to meet by their chairperson or at the request of at least two of their members, and at least twice a year. They will draw up an annual report on the subjects referred to them and on the opinions and recommendations given, which will be made available to any interested person and distributed to the journalists of the titles and sites concerned.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee of the daily newspaper <em>Le Monde</em>, its supplements or variations and the website lemonde.fr will be constituted and statutorily composed as follows, as specified in the shareholders' agreement between Le Monde Libre and the Pôle d'indépendance: two representatives of the Société des Rédacteurs du Monde (SRM); one representative of the Société des Rédacteurs du Monde Interactif (SRMIA); one representative of the Sociétés des Cadres et Employés du Monde; one representative of the Société des Lecteurs du <em>Monde</em>; the chairman of the board of directors of Le Monde SA (LMSA) or his delegate; the director of Le <em>Monde</em> or his delegate; the editorial director of Le <em>Monde</em> or his delegate; two qualified and independent public figures, appointed by the supervisory board of LMSA with the express agreement of the journalists' societies concerned (SRM and SRMIA); a representative of the Hubert Beuve-Méry Association or, in the event of the latter's dissolution, a qualified and independent figure, appointed by the Société des lecteurs du Monde and approved by SRM and SRMIA, who will chair the Committee.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">If necessary, and if the agenda of the session so requires, the directors of the publications or sites concerned may be heard.</p>          <div id="inread-17" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">In addition, whenever Le Monde.fr appears on the committee's agenda, the editorial director of Le Monde.fr will participate.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee of the Magazines Division will be constituted and statutorily composed as follows, as specified in the shareholders' agreement between Le Monde Libre and the Pôle d'indépendance: two representatives of SCP PVC; one representative of the Société de journalistes de <em>Télérama</em>; one representative of the Société de journalistes de <em>La Vie</em>; one representative of the Société de journalistes de <em>Courrier international</em>; the chairman of the board of directors of LMSA or his delegate; the editorial director of <em>Télérama</em>; the editorial director of <em>La Vie</em>; the editorial director of <em>Courrier international</em>; a qualified and independent figure, appointed by the LMSA supervisory board with the express agreement of the journalists' societies of the Magazines Division, who will chair the Committee; a member of the Georges-Hourdin Association (it being understood that they must not have previously held an executive position within a Group publication).</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">If necessary, and if the agenda of the session so requires, the directors of the publications or sites concerned may be heard.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">ETHICS COMMITTEE DOCUMENTS</p>               <p ">APPENDICES</p>              <h2 class="article__sub-title"><strong>Ethical principles</strong></h2>              <p class="article__paragraph  ">Interviews: Interviews published as "Questions and Answers" should not be read by the interviewees, or only for the purpose of avoiding factual or comprehension errors. If the interviewee substantially changes the content of their remarks, the author of the interview may, with the editorial director, refuse to publish the interview.</p>          <div id="inread-18" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Press trip: A press trip is a trip organized for promotional purposes and paid for by an outside organization. The use of press trips must be exceptional and professionally justified. Acceptance of a press trip should always be discussed with a line manager to determine the value and necessity of the trip. Any journalist may refuse to participate in a press trip without having to explain themselves. Participation in a press trip does not constitute a commitment on the part of the journalist or their editorial staff to publish an article resulting from it.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">The mention "Envoyé spécial" (Special Envoy) may only be used, in case of publication of an article, if the transportation costs have been paid by the newspaper concerned. Otherwise, only the place where the information was collected can be mentioned.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Gifts: Journalists agree to refuse any gift with a value of more than 70 euros, or of a nature that would call into question their independence. In case of products loaned for the purpose of writing an article, the products or materials may not be loaned for more than three months.</p>          <div id="inread-19" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p class="article__paragraph  ">Right of reply and corrections: The right of reply shall be published in accordance with the law. Any journalist concerned by the publication of a right of reply must be informed before the publication. The same goes for corrections.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Conflict of interest: The group's journalists refuse to cover a subject in which they have a personal conflict of interest. They will not cover a subject in which a member of their family or close circle of friends holds a position of authority. They do not buy shares in a company they follow for their newspaper.</p>               <p class="article__paragraph  ">Any review of a book or work whose author works regularly for the title or site that publishes it must mention their contributor status.</p>          <div id="inread-20" class="dfp-slot dfp__slot dfp__inread dfp-unloaded" data-format="inread" aria-hidden="true"></div>          <p About us About us About us Groupe Le Monde's Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct This Code came into effect on Tuesday, 2 November 2010. Le Monde Published on April 6, 2022, at 11:42 am (Paris) 17 min read Make us preferred on Google share Share on Messenger Share on Facebook Share by email Share on Linkedin Copy link Preamble Shareholders’ rights and obligations Governance Journalists’ rights and obligations Advertising Brand protection Role and power of journalists' organizations Role and power of ethics and professional conduct committees Appendix: Ethical principles Appendix: Declaration of interest Preamble The purpose of this Code is to recall the essential principles of independence, freedom and reliability of information, and to specify the rights and obligations of journalists, executives, and shareholders. It will be binding on the parties (organizations or associations of journalists of the various titles, shareholders, Groupe Le Monde executives, directors of publications and newsrooms), and will be included in the articles of association of Groupe Le Monde companies. In the event of a change in leadership of one of the group's titles, it will be imposed in identical terms on their new editorial and publishing directors. This Code, which is shared by all Groupe Le Monde publications and sites, is an addition to the charters and agreements previously adopted by each of these titles. These texts, which are joined in an appendix to this Code, remain fully valid with the only exception of any of their provisions that may be contradictory with those of the present Code. Any change to this Code must be approved by a vote of the publications and is effective only in those publications that have actually approved it. The vocation of Groupe Le Monde's titles is to provide, across all media, high-quality, accurate, verified and balanced information. Journalists must look at the news with a critical eye and reflect the pluralism of opinions. Journalists have the means needed to carry out their work with attention to detail, to collect and verify information, independently of any external pressure. They refrain from manipulation and plagiarism, do not spread hearsay, and avoid sensationalism, approximations and bias. They must avoid any ties of interest with the actors in the sectors they report on, and undertake to declare any conflict of interest. The ethical principles shared by the newsrooms of Groupe Le Monde will be set out in an appendix to the Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, without any distinction in value or legal force with the content of the latter. The editorial independence of Groupe Le Monde’s newspapers from its shareholders, advertisers, public, political, economic, ideological and religious authorities is the necessary condition for a free press and high-quality reporting. No text can be imposed on them, no direction can be dictated to them by an external intervention or constraint. The shareholders of Groupe Le Monde guarantee the economic independence of its titles within the meaning of the present Code, but refrain from interfering in their editorial choices and the way they handle information. The editorial policy of each title, whether in print or online, cannot be guided or influenced by the interests of advertisers, nor by those of other titles in the group. The editorial directors (or their delegates) are responsible for the editorial policy and content of their publication. Within each title of Groupe Le Monde, there is a person responsible for the title’s economic equilibrium and management, who is separate from the person responsible for the editorial content. Under no circumstances may one of these two managers make a decision that affects the other's area of responsibility without the latter's agreement. Two separate ethics and professional conduct committees, responsible respectively for the Le Monde daily newspaper, its supplements or variations, the Le Monde Interactif websites and its digital applications, on the one hand, and for all the magazines (the "Magazines Division") and their digital editions, on the other, are responsible for ensuring compliance with this Code. In particular, they will ensure that all the principles contained in the Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists (Munich, 1971), which is essential to ensuring editorial independence and constitutes the ethical basis of the journalistic profession, are observed. These principles apply to the production of all editorial content produced by the group's newsrooms, regardless of the media used. This Code will be published in whole or in part in the various titles of the group as soon as it comes into force and will remain available in full and at any time on each of their websites. Shareholders’ rights and obligations The shareholders of Groupe Le Monde hold the powers conferred on them by corporate law. In this capacity, they oversee the smooth operations of the group and its publications, and help define its strategy and areas of development. To ensure the financial and political independence of the group's titles and sites, and to guarantee their independence and freedom of expression, each of them agrees to respect the values and principles defined in this Code. The shareholders hereby attest to their commitment to the editorial independence of the group’s publications. They agree to respect this Code, as well as the specific charters in use in each of the group's newsrooms. Any new shareholder, whether majority or minority, will have to make the same commitment. The companies in Groupe Le Monde may only register movements or subscriptions of securities giving access to the capital in return for the adherence and signature of the present Code by their beneficiaries. The shareholders, their representatives and the members of the supervisory boards of Groupe Le Monde do not take part in editorial decisions. They attend editorial conferences only at the invitation of the newsroom or the newspaper's management, but may not speak at these meetings. They also refrain from commissioning an article and from giving instructions to modify an article or preventing it from being published. The shareholding structure of Groupe Le Monde will be published annually in paper and/or digital form by each of the Group's titles. At the same time, a report on the interests held by the main shareholders will also be provided. The shareholders agree not to impose commercial partnerships on the Group with companies they are shareholders in or which are tied to them through commercial relations. Similarly, they agree not to prevent or hinder similar partnerships with companies that are in competition with their own. When a shareholder of Groupe Le Monde or a company managed or owned by one of these shareholders is quoted in an article published by a title of Groupe Le Monde, this is indicated in the body of the article, in its title, or in a footnote. Governance Shareholders and members of the supervisory boards agree to ensure that, in the context of public expression, their statements may not be taken as the opinion of Groupe Le Monde, except in the case of a communication voted on by the supervisory board. Membership in a Group Management Board is incompatible with: - a national or local elective mandate (except for municipal mandates in cities with fewer than 30,000 residents) - a management, supervisory or representative role within a political party or trade union - a final prison sentence related to the following subjects: (i) incitement to racial hatred or discrimination; (ii) illicit financing of political parties; (iii) personal injury. Journalists’ rights and obligations This Code recognizes the Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists, adopted in Munich in 1971, in the following terms: Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists Preamble The right to information, free expression and criticism is one of the most fundamental freedoms of every human being. The whole complex of duties and rights of journalists derives from this right of the public to know facts and opinions. The responsibility of journalists vis-a-vis the public has precedence over any other responsibility, in particular towards their employers and the public power. The mission to inform necessarily includes the limits journalists spontaneously impose on themselves. This is the subject of the present declaration of duties. Yet these duties can be effectively respected in the exercise of the journalist profession only if the concrete conditions of professional independence and dignity are implemented. This is the subject of the declaration of rights quoted here. Declaration of Duties The essential duties of the journalist in gathering, reporting on and commenting on events consist in: 1) Respecting the truth no matter what consequences it may bring about to him, and this is because the right of the public is to know the truth. 2) Defending the freedom of information, of commentaries and of criticism. 3) Publishing only such pieces of information the origin of which is known or – in the opposite case – accompanying them with due reservations; not suppressing essential information and not altering texts and documents. 4) Not making use of disloyal methods to get information, photographs and documents. 5) Feeling obliged to respect the private life of people. 6) Correcting any published information which has proved to be inaccurate. 7) Observing professional secrecy and not divulging the source of information obtained confidentially. 8) Abstaining from plagiarism, slander, defamation and unfounded accusations as well as from receiving any advantage owing to the publication or suppression of information. 9) Never confusing the profession of journalist with that of advertiser or propagandist and not accepting any consideration, direct or not, from advertisers. 10) Refusing any pressure and accepting editorial directives only from the leading persons in charge in the editorial office. Every journalist worthy of that name deems it his duty faithfully to observe the principles stated above. Within the general law of each country, the journalist recognizes, in professional matters, the jurisdiction of his colleagues only; he excludes every kind of interference by governments or others. Declaration of Rights 1) Journalists claim free access to all information sources, and the right to freely inquire on all events conditioning public life. Therefore, secrecy of public or private affairs may be opposed only to journalists in exceptional cases and for clearly expressed motives. 2) The journalist has the right to refuse subordination to anything contrary to the general policy of the information organ to which he collaborates such as it has been laid down in writing and incorporated in his contract of employment, as well as any subordination not clearly implicated by this general policy. 3) A journalist cannot be compelled to perform a professional act or to express an opinion contrary to his convictions or his conscience. 4) The editorial staff has obligatorily to be informed on all important decisions which may influence the life of the enterprise. It should at least be consulted before a definitive decision on all matters related to the composition of the editorial staff, e.g. recruitment, dismissals, mutations and promotion of journalists, is taken. 5) Taking into account his functions and responsibilities, the journalist is entitled not only to the advantages resulting from collective agreements but also to an individual contract of employment, ensuring the material and moral security of his work as well as a wage system corresponding to his social condition and guaranteeing his economic independence Advertising In each of Groupe Le Monde's titles, whether in print or digital format, as well as in their supplements or special issues, editorial space and advertising or promotional space must be clearly and unambiguously marked. The typography, iconography and layout of advertising or advertorials must not be confused with the editorial content. Advertising imperatives cannot be invoked to influence the editorial choices of Groupe Le Monde's titles. Journalists may not contribute, even anonymously or free of charge, to the design, writing, illustration or layout of an advertisement or advertorial published in one of the group's titles. Advertisers have no right to review or intervene in the content, including in supplements and special issues that they have helped to finance. Brand protection Groupe Le Monde's brands must not be used in a way that is incompatible with the Group's values. The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees shall assess and judge any risk of damage to the image of the brand concerned. In the event of an agreement entailing a risk of this type, the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Société éditrice du Monde (SEM) (or, if it is separate from the SEM, the legal representative of the parent company of the Magazine Division) must refer the matter to the relevant Ethics Committee, within a period of time that will allow it to give its opinion before any irrevocable commitment is made. If this is not the case, any of its members may refer the matter to the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. The Committee may prohibit any use of the brand, outside the communication and media sector, which it considers detrimental to the image of the brand. Role and power of journalists' organizations An elected representative body, the board of the journalists' societies (SDJ) or their equivalent (journalists' associations, editors' organizations, etc.) of each publication has as its natural and permanent point of contact the editorial director of its title. In the event of a dispute, they may refer the matter to the appropriate Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. When faced with a problem of an ethical nature, any journalist has the right to refer the matter to her SDJ’s office so that it may become aware of it and submit it to the editorial director in order to find a solution. The editorial director and the publication director may also refer it to the SDJ office. The SDJ of a publication is informed in advance, within a reasonable period of time, of any decision relating to the development strategy of the title (in particular the creation or acquisition of a website, audiovisual support and a new product or a new activity). In the event of a proposed change of formula, the SDJ is informed by the editorial director or the publication director. In the event of proposed modifications to the production circuit, and after informing the elected representatives of the personnel, the editorial director will inform the relevant SDJ. Role and power of ethics and professional conduct committees The purpose of the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees, to which the articles of association of the companies of Groupe Le Monde expressly refer, is to ensure compliance with this Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct within the Group’s various publications and sites. They do not have the authority to rule on the content of an article, nor to impose sanctions on journalists. In the event of a dispute over the interpretation or application of the Code, the matter may be referred to the relevant Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee by two of its members, by an SDJ, the editorial director or the chairman of the board of directors. Within one month of the referral, and after having interviewed the persons of its choice, the Committee shall issue an opinion and/or recommendations which will be communicated to the journalists concerned, to the management of the newsroom concerned and to the Chairman of the Board of Directors, and which may be published at its request. The management of the title concerned shall to respond in detail, and within fifteen days, to the opinion or recommendations of the Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committees shall be summoned to meet by their chairperson or at the request of at least two of their members, and at least twice a year. They will draw up an annual report on the subjects referred to them and on the opinions and recommendations given, which will be made available to any interested person and distributed to the journalists of the titles and sites concerned. The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee of the daily newspaper Le Monde , its supplements or variations and the website lemonde.fr will be constituted and statutorily composed as follows, as specified in the shareholders' agreement between Le Monde Libre and the Pôle d'indépendance: two representatives of the Société des Rédacteurs du Monde (SRM); one representative of the Société des Rédacteurs du Monde Interactif (SRMIA); one representative of the Sociétés des Cadres et Employés du Monde; one representative of the Société des Lecteurs du Monde ; the chairman of the board of directors of Le Monde SA (LMSA) or his delegate; the director of Le Monde or his delegate; the editorial director of Le Monde or his delegate; two qualified and independent public figures, appointed by the supervisory board of LMSA with the express agreement of the journalists' societies concerned (SRM and SRMIA); a representative of the Hubert Beuve-Méry Association or, in the event of the latter's dissolution, a qualified and independent figure, appointed by the Société des lecteurs du Monde and approved by SRM and SRMIA, who will chair the Committee. If necessary, and if the agenda of the session so requires, the directors of the publications or sites concerned may be heard. In addition, whenever Le Monde.fr appears on the committee's agenda, the editorial director of Le Monde.fr will participate. The Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee of the Magazines Division will be constituted and statutorily composed as follows, as specified in the shareholders' agreement between Le Monde Libre and the Pôle d'indépendance: two representatives of SCP PVC; one representative of the Société de journalistes de Télérama ; one representative of the Société de journalistes de La Vie ; one representative of the Société de journalistes de Courrier international ; the chairman of the board of directors of LMSA or his delegate; the editorial director of Télérama ; the editorial director of La Vie ; the editorial director of Courrier international ; a qualified and independent figure, appointed by the LMSA supervisory board with the express agreement of the journalists' societies of the Magazines Division, who will chair the Committee; a member of the Georges-Hourdin Association (it being understood that they must not have previously held an executive position within a Group publication). If necessary, and if the agenda of the session so requires, the directors of the publications or sites concerned may be heard. APPENDICES Ethical principles Interviews: Interviews published as "Questions and Answers" should not be read by the interviewees, or only for the purpose of avoiding factual or comprehension errors. If the interviewee substantially changes the content of their remarks, the author of the interview may, with the editorial director, refuse to publish the interview. Press trip: A press trip is a trip organized for promotional purposes and paid for by an outside organization. The use of press trips must be exceptional and professionally justified. Acceptance of a press trip should always be discussed with a line manager to determine the value and necessity of the trip. Any journalist may refuse to participate in a press trip without having to explain themselves. Participation in a press trip does not constitute a commitment on the part of the journalist or their editorial staff to publish an article resulting from it. The mention "Envoyé spécial" (Special Envoy) may only be used, in case of publication of an article, if the transportation costs have been paid by the newspaper concerned. Otherwise, only the place where the information was collected can be mentioned. Gifts: Journalists agree to refuse any gift with a value of more than 70 euros, or of a nature that would call into question their independence. In case of products loaned for the purpose of writing an article, the products or materials may not be loaned for more than three months. Right of reply and corrections: The right of reply shall be published in accordance with the law. Any journalist concerned by the publication of a right of reply must be informed before the publication. The same goes for corrections. Conflict of interest: The group's journalists refuse to cover a subject in which they have a personal conflict of interest. They will not cover a subject in which a member of their family or close circle of friends holds a position of authority. They do not buy shares in a company they follow for their newspaper. Any review of a book or work whose author works regularly for the title or site that publishes it must mention their contributor status. Note: Other editorial principles may be included in the texts and charters that are specific to the group's various titles.
